STRATEGY: Parent slot 11 is a 100-round IPD strategy with no execution noise; the trace simulates opponents including always-C, always-D, TFT, forgiving, and exploitative strategies. It plans to start C, probe with D when the opponent has never defected, exploit unconditional cooperators, use forgiving TFT-like logic otherwise, and defect in the last two rounds.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: The parent is a tournament strategy that starts cooperatively, probes/exploits unconditional cooperators, retaliates against defection, forgives when it caused the opponent's defection, and defects in the endgame. The trace simulates variants against TFT, always-C, always-D, probers, alternating, and late-switching opponents. It changes the strategy to exploit when opp_defects==0, use recent/overall cooperation rates, forgive if it defected in the last two rounds, and defect on the last two rounds.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says: 'Consider beginning cooperatively to make mutual cooperation possible. Give a partner opportunities to return to a mutually cooperative interaction. Avoid allowing an isolated defection to cause permanent mutual retaliation.' This suggests we should not be too exploitative."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates early, retaliates when opponent defects, forgives with randomness, and defects in the endgame. The trace simulates aggressive early exploitation, Grim Trigger, slot 3, TFT, always-C, and always-D. It changes toward cooperating for the first 10 rounds, continuing cooperation when opp_defects==0, and defecting only in the last two rounds.

It changes the early cooperation phase to 10 rounds, adds a clearer forgiveness rule, and keeps a last-two-rounds defect.
